body:
F0 FIXTURE CONTRACT V3 — NARROW SYNTHESIS REPAIR AFTER TWO INDEPENDENT V2 AMEND REVIEWS. DESIGN/ADMISSION SPECIFICATION ONLY; NO GENERATION, MEDIA, DEPENDENCY, RUNTIME, OR AUTHORIZATION.

The project-authored F0 is a receipted fixture family with independent authorities. It is not one movie, one tool validating itself, or a vehicle for parser/security or narrative claims.

## A. Closed artifact classes

Every artifact, manifest, receipt, cache key, mutation, and result carries an unforgeable class identity.

1. `ValidMedia.BasicAv`: legal AV/VFR member with repeated identical picture samples, a hard physical discontinuity, a gradual physical transition, explicit tone, and decoded all-zero PCM silence. It carries no narrative labels.
2. `ValidMedia.LeadingPictureGap`: separate member in which edition playback begins with audio while picture has a declared leading empty edit/no-correspondence interval. Stock MOV-writer feasibility is limited to this leading form. Interior edit-list gaps, native timestamp/sample gaps, held final samples, and absent samples are separate phenomena and require separate members/evidence if claimed.
3. `ValidMedia.TimedTextSidecar`: exact sidecar format and reader with cue gaps. Embedded MOV text is a separate optional variant with its own tag, muxer, demuxer, and decoder closure.
4. `ValidMedia.LumaMetric`: analytically simple constant-color/luma schedule whose expected arithmetic is independently computed for one exact ContentDetector recipe. It tests raw metric plumbing only.
5. `SyntheticAdapterMutation`: provider-free envelopes, each paired with a nearby valid control, for packet-field AV_NOPTS, rescale overflow yielding the same raw INT64_MIN, PASS_MINMAX provenance, present PTS below DTS, unknown duration, negative origin, epoch collision, quantization/refusal, set-valued reverse, occurrence loss, and gap-bridging mutations. These are not media bytes and cannot enter media coverage or provider metrics.
6. `CourtMutation`: in-scope negative artifacts with typed subkind `ContainerLayout | Payload | Sidecar | Oracle | Cache`. Each binds base artifact digest, mutation kind and location, expected detecting court, and mutated digest; it cannot retain `ValidMedia` identity. `ContainerLayout` bytes are project-authored and are passed only to the independent layout validator, never to the target reader. Their sole ceiling is killing the validator's declared subset.
7. `MalformedContainer`: deferred and out of F0. Actual target-demux, truncation, malformed-input, parser-robustness, or security claims require a separately admitted corpus. Synthetic failures and validator-only mutations cannot establish them.

## B. Independent authority leaves

1. `Intent`: canonical schema/version/hash; edition extent; complete stream roster; rational timebases/origins/epochs/occurrences; sample identities and PTS/DTS/duration presence; mappings; gaps; timed-text cues; visual/audio schedules; physical transition intervals; expected typed support/refusal outcomes. Expected logical samples, coordinates, mappings, and payload hashes exist before generation.
2. `AuthoritativeGenerator`: exact project source, licence/notices, runtime, toolchain, dependencies, environment contract, and digest. It uses no FFmpeg/libav writer implementation lineage. A separately admitted FFmpeg writer may generate an auxiliary differential fixture, but it cannot satisfy the independent-generator court, manufacture the oracle, or share artifacts/runtime with the target reader. No wall clock, randomness, locale, timezone, filesystem order, hostname, network, or undeclared environment input may affect authoritative bytes.
3. `ContainerLayoutValidator`: an implementation/code path independent of AuthoritativeGenerator and target MOV reader. It validates only its declared subset. Until realized, “standards-valid” remains held. A generator-authored layout receipt and successful target demux are not independent validation.
4. `SemanticOracle`: separate implementation and cache identity from AuthoritativeGenerator, ContainerLayoutValidator, ReaderClosure, PixelHandoff, and BoundaryProvider. It may share canonical schemas and one declared digest primitive, but shares no decoder, rescale, mapping, conversion, transition, or metric implementation whose output it judges. It establishes intent-derived logical schedules, mappings, sample hashes, tone/silence/text expectations, and physical transition intervals—not container legality, reader correctness, or detector quality.
5. `ReaderClosure`: exact MOV demuxer plus only manifest-selected rawvideo, PCM, and timed-text readers. PCM binds endian/width/tag, rate, channels/layout, packet/sample framing, and duration semantics. The landed probe-only FFmpeg recipe admits none of these decoders.
6. `PixelHandoff`: held alternatives until pinned conformance selects one: MOV `24BG` -> BGR24 direct decode plus receipted handoff normalizer, or MOV `raw ` -> RGB24 plus separately admitted deterministic RGB-to-BGR bridge. FFmpeg table membership is feasibility evidence only. Both routes bind fourcc, pixel format, dimensions, stride/padding, row orientation, color metadata, buffer ownership/lifetime, per-sample input/output hashes, occurrence identity, and fail-closed unsupported layouts. Direct BGR removes channel permutation, not handoff accountability.
7. `BoundaryProvider`: exact PySceneDetect ContentDetector recipe and preprocessing identity. It consumes only receipted BGR samples by source sample ID and never owns source timestamps.

## C. Two aligned coverage layers

Stream capability is `Decoded | PacketIndexedOnly | Unsupported`; capability is not coverage and `Unsupported` is not relabelled `Unexamined`.

1. Reader coverage is a complete, nonoverlapping edition-extent partition using applicable states such as `DecodedSupport`, `PacketOnlySupport`, `UnsupportedByReader`, `NoCorrespondingSample`, `ProcessingFailure`, and `ReaderUnexamined`. `OutsideDomain` remains a mapping-query outcome, not a catch-all for unsupported, gap, failure, or unexamined support.
2. Boundary-provider search coverage is a separate partition aligned to reader coverage. Decoded picture support can be `ProviderExamined`, `ProviderFailed`, `ProviderAbstained`, or `ProviderUnexamined`; non-decoded picture extent is explicitly ineligible. Provider results separately distinguish candidates from `ExaminedNoCandidate`. Empty output over partial, failed, abstained, ineligible, or unexamined coverage is never negative evidence.

Mandatory distinct cases include: no audio stream; unsupported audio reader; audio mapping gap; decoded all-zero PCM silence; unknown sample duration; decode failure; equal frame hashes with distinct occurrence IDs; held final picture sample versus picture gap; cue gap versus absent, unsupported, or failed text track; clean EOS versus typed processing failure; and continuing audio while edition-to-picture mapping returns no correspondence without endpoint bridging. Actual truncated-byte behavior remains deferred to `MalformedContainer`.

## D. Determinism, mutation, tamper, and cache courts

Two isolated clean runs with no reused cache must produce the same ordered output digest set; otherwise byte determinism is unproven. Request identity binds intent/schema, generator source, toolchain/platform/dependency closure, ordered output manifest, oracle implementation/digest, validator identity, and reader/bridge/preprocessing/provider recipes. Host/time diagnostics are attempt metadata, not scientific identity.

Separate receipts cover generation, byte replay, oracle correctness, layout conformance, demux/decode conformance, pixel handoff, both coverage layers, raw boundary metrics/proposals, and provider replay. Typed `CourtMutation`s independently alter one generated timestamp, one pixel/audio/cue payload, one sidecar, one oracle hash, one cache entry, or one declared layout constraint. Each must fail only its expected court; validator-only layout mutations never reach ReaderClosure. Cache-poisoning and equal-request/unequal-output cases fail. These courts prove only their named contracts, never general parser security.

## E. Boundary and claim ceiling

Physical hard/gradual transition intervals are oracle facts about generated pixels, not narrative scenes and not prescribed detector proposals. Complete provider examination with zero proposals yields `ExaminedNoCandidate` for one exact recipe—not physical no-transition evidence. Candidate, complete-no-candidate, partial, failed, abstained, ineligible, and unexamined outcomes remain distinct. The luma member may prove independently checkable raw metric plumbing; it proves no proposal quality, calibration, morphology, or localization accuracy.

F0 may prove only authoritative-generator byte determinism, declared-subset layout conformance, intent-oracle agreement, exact stream inventory, time/mapping/refusal preservation, decoded sample and pixel-handoff identity, complete reader/provider coverage accounting, boundary measurement/proposal plumbing, typed tamper detection, and replay. It proves no ASR, speaker, face, character, action, event, scene, causality, narrative, recall, model quality, target-parser robustness, or security claim.

This V3 accepts V1/V2 AMEND records post-01M19KRY0VQ9ZH6DMEXWC2HZV5, post-01M19KWNBTW5M9DYFSQQ0X8RJ6, post-01M19M3FHATFE6CK9DXXXMYR09, and post-01M19M63RACC0S580RVP1N4TR0. It supersedes V2. Exact physical manifests and component realizations remain future admission decisions. If both reviewers confirm this exact synthesis, flag it for routing as the B0-C F0 generator/fixture specification; do not modify D2 V8 or start implementation.

Reviewers: ACCEPT / AMEND / BLOCK this exact V3. No response grants authority.
